Report Title: Evaluation of Alignment Between Large Language Models and Expert Clinicians in Suicide Risk Assessment
Finding: Across 9,000 responses to 30 clinician-rated suicide-related queries, RAND found ChatGPT answered very-low-risk queries directly 100% of the time and never answered a very-high-risk query directly, but did not meaningfully distinguish low-, medium- and high-risk queries in between.

Report Title: AI agents put offensive cyber within reach of novices: Comparing the performance of AI agents to humans in offensive cyber operations
Models / Systems: Claude Code with Claude Sonnet and Claude Opus 4.6 (Anthropic)
Finding: Re-running CTF challenges on which human participants (novices and technically advanced users) had previously shown statistically insignificant uplift from August 2025 chatbots over eight hours, RAND found Claude Code with Sonnet and Opus 4.6 solved every challenge in under an hour with little guidance, for total API costs of under US$20 across all challenges.
Finding Quote: Following this study we re-tested the same challenges with Claude Code using Sonnet and Opus 4.6. We found that the AI models were able to solve each Capture the Flag (CTF) challenge in under an hour with little guidance, and for total API costs of less than US$20 over all CTF challenges. Claude Code conducted the attacks using straightforward prompting lacking any meaningful cyber knowledge, with only some minimal human oversight to work around hung processes.

Report Title: AI agents put offensive cyber within reach of novices: Comparing the performance of AI agents to humans in offensive cyber operations
Models / Systems: anonymised (two different AI models in RAND's CTF runs)
Finding: RAND observed one AI model piggy-backing on a target system that a different AI model had already partially exploited, reusing that prior progress to save time and cost - a behaviour they note could let agents exploit partially patched systems faster than benchmarks suggest and complicate attribution.
Finding Quote: We observed one AI model taking advantage of the progress a previous and different AI model had made, saving time and money. If vulnerable systems are only partially patched or if cybersecurity incidents are not fully resolved, AI agents may be able to exploit such systems at rate faster and cheaper than benchmarks and further complicate attribution.

Finding: RAND concludes that CTF-style and passive-vulnerable-system evaluations may be approaching saturation and that relevant offensive-cyber assessments now need environments with active defenders who can detect and counter an attack.
